title: Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism

paragraphs.en: Traditionally, rabbit breeding focused on wool and fur production, utilizing breeds such as Angora and Rex.1 Recently, however, meat production has gained significance, particularly with the New Zealand and Californian breeds, due to the favourable nutritional profile of rabbit meat compared to that of conventional livestock.2 Rabbit meat is lean, contains lower overall fat, and has a beneficial fatty acid composition. Its MF is enriched with lecithin and unsaturated lipids, which enhance tenderness, juiciness, and flavor.3 These qualities have spurred interest in the biological mechanisms that regulate meat quality in rabbits.

Research characterizing intramuscular preadipocytes and establishing reliable isolation and differentiation protocols is well advanced in major livestock species such as pigs, cattle, and chickens. In contrast, comparable studies in rabbits remain limited. While pioneering work has demonstrated the adipogenic potential of rabbit adipose-derived stem cells (ASCs) and mesenchymal stem cells, these studies have primarily focused on subcutaneous and visceral depots,4,5 leaving the intramuscular compartment largely unexplored. A notable exception is the study ,6 which compared intramuscular and subcutaneous preadipocytes in New Zealand rabbits, revealing depot-specific differences in adipogenic potential. Although very close, this study had several important limitations: it lacked comprehensive phenotypic characterization of the isolated cells as bona fide preadipocytes before differentiation, such as through surface marker profiling or rigorous exclusion of fibroblast or myoblast contamination. Furthermore, the differentiation process and the resulting adipocytes were not thoroughly quantified using modern molecular endpoints, such as time-course analysis of key adipogenic markers (e.g., PPARG, CEBPA, FABP4, and ADIPOQ). Similarly, the work of7 primarily focused on comparing lipid metabolism and adipocyte characteristics in rabbit lines with divergent IMF content. While the study provided valuable preliminary observations on adipocyte size and metabolic enzyme activities, it did not detail or standardize protocols for the isolation of intramuscular adipocytes, nor did it present a comprehensive molecular validation framework for these cells.

Furthermore, emerging rabbit transcriptomic studies support the existence of strong depot-specific regulatory programs, with perirenal (visceral) adipose tissue showing distinct adipogenesis-related miRNA regulation.8,9 At the same time, IMF deposition is shaped by muscle-based transcriptional and long non-coding RNA (lncRNA)–mRNA networks linked to pathways such as PPAR, Wnt, and TGF-β.10,11 Investigations into perirenal adipose tissue have characterized gene expression, miRNA profiles, and metabolic responses, demonstrating its role in energy storage with distinct regulatory signatures.12,13 Recent transcriptomic and epigenetic analyses further indicate that IMF possesses a unique regulatory network, marked by differential m6A methylation patterns and expression of key adipogenic genes and methylases.14,15 Furthermore, lipogenic enzyme activities and adipocyte characteristics differ significantly between these depots.16 Together, these findings indicate that fat deposition is regulated differently across visceral and intramuscular compartments in rabbits.

Despite these insights, no study has directly isolated and optimized a culture system for intramuscular preadipocytes in rabbits, a methodological gap that is particularly critical given that rabbits exhibit unique metabolic characteristics as hindgut fermenters, distinct from both monogastric and ruminant species.17 Developing a reliable in vitro culture system for rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes (IMPA) would not only facilitate exploration of adipogenesis in this species but also enable investigation into the regulatory roles of lncRNAs, transcription factors, and microbiota-derived metabolites in IMF development. This methodological gap impedes mechanistic research on rabbit intramuscular adipogenesis and its implications for meat quality. To address this, our study was designed to establish and comprehensively characterize a standardized in vitro model system for rabbit IMPA. We specifically focus on developing a robust isolation and culture protocol from a neonatal source, ensuring a consistent and viable cell population for foundational studies. The primary aim is not to characterize the in vivo IMPA population at slaughter age, but to develop and validate an essential in vitro tool. By optimizing enzymatic digestion and culture conditions and providing comprehensive morphological and molecular validation (including the expression of key adipogenic markers), we establish the identity and adipogenic potential of rabbit IMPAs. This work lays critical groundwork for subsequent investigations into the molecular and nutritional regulation of IMF deposition in rabbits, offering a direct methodological foundation for meat science and genetic improvement strategies.

DMEM-F12 high glucose medium and sterile PBS were obtained from Shanghai Peiyuan Biotechnology Co., Ltd., China. Fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 3-isobutyl 1-methylxanthine (IBMX) were sourced from Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA. Penicillin/streptomycin (double antibody), dexamethasone (DEX), insulin, type I and type II collagenase were purchased from Sanya Solebao Biotechnology Co., Ltd., Hainan Sheng, China. The Oil Red O staining kit was obtained from the Biosun company, China. The RNA extraction kit was acquired from Meiji Seika Pharma Co., Ltd., Japan, while reverse transcription and quantification kits were sourced from Takara, Dalian, China. Additional reagents included Triton X-100 (BIO BASIN, Shanghai, China), bovine serum albumin (Biosciences, Franklin Lakes, New Jersey, USA), and DAPI (Bioss, Beijing, China).

Three male Hycole rabbits aged 3 days were collected from the rabbit farm of Northwest A&F University, Yangling, Shaanxi, China. The use of 3-day-old neonates was selected for initial protocol development based on their higher progenitor cell abundance and tissue accessibility, which facilitates method optimization and ensures consistent cell yields for establishing the standardized protocol.18–20 All animal experiments followed ARRIVE guidelines as approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) of Northwest A&F University (Approval No. 202205A29). Rabbits were fasted for 12 hours before euthanasia with free access to water to ensure animal welfare during the fasting period. Following fasting, rabbits were euthanized via intravenous injection of sodium pentobarbital (50 mg/kg body weight) administered through the marginal ear vein after ensuring adequate anaesthesia through the absence of pedal reflexes. A section of the longissimus dorsi (LD) muscle was aseptically excised using sterile surgical scissors and a scalpel under laminar flow conditions. The excised tissue was immediately transferred to sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) containing 2% penicillin-streptomycin to minimize microbial contamination. Intramuscular preadipocytes were subsequently isolated from this muscle section using enzymatic digestion and differential centrifugation procedures, as described below.

sections.title: Isolation and culture of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes

paragraphs.en: The isolation workflow is illustrated in Figure 1. LD muscle tissue was excised aseptically and washed alternately with PBS containing 2% penicillin/streptomycin. Visible blood vessels and fascia were carefully removed using sterile scissors and scalpels, and the muscle was minced into 1–3 mm³ fragments. Tissue fragments were digested with type I collagenase (2 mg/mL) at 37 °C for 90 minutes in a shaking water bath. Digestion was terminated with an equal volume of DMEM/F12 supplemented with 10% foetal bovine serum (FBS). The digest was sequentially filtered through 70 µm and 40 µm sieves to remove debris, and the filtrate was centrifuged at 1200 rpm for 10 minutes to obtain the stromal vascular cell pellet.

The resulting cell fraction, which represents a heterogeneous stromal population enriched in preadipocytes, was resuspended in prewarmed (37 °C) DMEM/F12 and washed twice by centrifugation (1200 rpm, 5 minutes). Cells were seeded at 2 × 104 cells/cm2 in tissue culture–treated plastic dishes with complete culture medium (DMEM high glucose medium, 15% FBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin) and incubated at 37 °C with 5% CO2. After 48 hours, adherent cells were maintained in culture and expanded up to passage 3 (P3) for subsequent analyses.

It is acknowledged that this protocol yields a mixed stromal vascular cell population rather than a fully purified preadipocyte population. However, preadipocytes are selectively enriched by their adherence, proliferation, and subsequent adipogenic differentiation capacity in vitro, which will be confirmed by our subsequent downstream experiments. Based on the literature, the isolated population is expected to consist predominantly of preadipocytes (60–70%) with stromal cells, including fibroblasts (20–30%), and minor populations of endothelial cells and immune cells (<10%).14,15

The immunofluorescence procedure was performed as previously described.21 IMPA were seeded in 6-well culture plates. Once the cell confluence reached 50–70%, the culture medium was discarded, and the cells were washed gently with PBS. Each well was treated with 4% paraformaldehyde to fix the cells for 30 minutes, followed by a PBS wash. The cells were permeabilized using 0.1% Triton X-100 for 60 minutes. After discarding the permeabilization solution, the cells were washed with PBS and blocked with 1% bovine serum albumin for 60 minutes. The blocking solution was removed, and diluted preadipocyte and adipocyte marker antibodies were added: rabbit preadipocyte factor 1 (anti-PREF-1, 1:200; Abcam, ab21682), anti-Leptin (1:200; Abcam, ab16227), and Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor Gamma (anti-PPARG, 1:500; Cell Signaling Technology, #3544). Scale bars (100 µm) were added to all images for reference. Each sample included three biological replicates (n = 3).

sections.title: Molecular characterization of isolated SVF and fibroblasts

paragraphs.en: Due to the lack of commercially available, validated antibodies against rabbit epitopes for key markers (PDGFRA, CD34, ITGA7), cell population characterization was performed using quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) to assess gene expression profiles. Total RNA was isolated from freshly harvested IMF-SVF and from P3 dermal fibroblasts using the Meiji Seika RNA Extraction kit. Gene expression was normalized to ACTB (β-actin) and analysed using the 2^(-ΔΔCt) method.

IMPA were plated in 96-well plates, with 6 × 10³ cells in each well. The CCK-8 method was used to evaluate the proliferation rate of the preadipocytes following the manufacturer’s protocol (Dojindo Molecular Technologies, Kumamoto, Japan) as previously described.22 Briefly, 10% CCK-8 reagent was added to each well, followed by incubation at 37 °C for 2 hours. The optical density (OD) value was then measured at a wavelength of 450 nm using a microplate reader.

IMPA grew to 90% confluence and continued to be cultured for 2 days. Then the complete culture medium was replaced with differentiation medium (DMEM/F12, supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 5 µg/mL (872 nmol/L) insulin, 1 µmol/L dexamethasone, and 0.5 mmol/L isobutyl methylxanthine (IBMX)). After two days of differentiation, the maintenance medium (DMEM/F12 containing 10% FBS and 1 µg/mL insulin) was used to replace the differentiation medium and maintain the cells for an additional 10 days. The cells were harvested at 0, 3, 6, and 9 days after induction and used for gene expression studies. Each stage included three biological replicates (n = 3). The detailed procedure for the induction of IMPA is described in Figure 2.

After the IMPA differentiated into recognizable lipid droplets, Oil Red O staining and quantification were conducted as previously described.6 The medium was discarded, and the cells were gently washed twice with PBS. Then, 1.5 mL of 10% neutral paraformaldehyde fixative was added to each well and incubated at room temperature for 30 minutes. Scale bars (200 µm) and magnification information (200×) were added to all images. For lipid quantification, the Oil Red O was eluted with 100% isopropanol and measured at 450 nm.

sections.title: RNA extraction and qRT-PCR detection of genes related to adipogenic differentiation

paragraphs.en: Total RNA was extracted from IMPA cells at 0, 3, 6, and 9 days of differentiation using an RNA extraction kit. RT-qPCR analysis was conducted as previously described.23 In brief, total RNA was isolated with TRIzol Reagent (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA). The integrity (quantity and quality) of the extracted RNA was assessed by measuring the optical density at 260 nm and calculating the ratio of the optical densities (OD) at 260/280 using a Nano Quant plate (TECAN, Infinite M200 PRO), and this was further verified using a 1% agarose gel. Reverse transcription was performed with the PrimeScript RT Reagent Kit, including gDNA Eraser (TaKaRa, Dalian, China), following the manufacturer’s protocol for the SYBR Premix EX Taq Kit (Takara, Dalian, China) on a thermocycler 7500 system (SDS V 1.4.0, Applied Biosystem, Waltham, MA, USA). Two-step qPCR was conducted using SYBR Green I (TaKaRa, Dalian, China). The thermocycling conditions included a pre-heating step at 95 ◦C for 5 minutes, followed by 34 cycles consisting of denaturation at 95 ◦C for 30 seconds, annealing at 60 ◦C for 30 seconds, and extension at 72 ◦C for 30 seconds. All assays were performed according to the manufacturer’s protocols. The expression level of the target gene was normalized using the β-actin gene.24 Details of the primers used are provided in Table S1. The relative expression level of the candidate gene was calculated using the cycle threshold 2^(-ΔΔCt) method, with three replicates conducted for each sample.

Data are presented as the mean ± standard deviation (SD). Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS software (Version 19.0; IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). The significance of differences among groups was assessed by one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), followed by Tukey’s honestly significant difference (HSD) post-hoc test for multiple comparisons. When numerous pairwise comparisons were performed within a single experimental context, the Holm-Šídák correction was applied to control the family-wise error rate.25 A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. All graphs were generated using GraphPad Prism software (Version 8.5; GraphPad Software, Inc., San Diego, CA, USA), and data are presented as mean ± SD, as indicated in all figure legends.

sections.title: Isolation efficiency, cell viability, and proliferation dynamics

paragraphs.en: The optimized collagenase digestion protocol yielded approximately 1.2 × 106 viable cells per gram of rabbit LD tissue, with a mean viability of 84% as determined by Trypan Blue staining. These values indicate high isolation efficiency relative to reports from other livestock species, despite the naturally low adipocyte density of rabbit muscle. Establishing such yield and viability benchmarks is therefore a critical methodological advancement for rabbit intramuscular adipose research. The high yield value obtained could be attributed to the use of neonatal tissue, as the neonatal period is critical for muscle and adipose tissue development, making neonatal tissues ideal for studying early adipogenic events and regulatory mechanisms,20,26 providing a higher proportion of progenitor cells and less fibrotic or mature muscle, facilitating more efficient isolation and culture of adipogenic cells18

To evaluate the viability and growth characteristics of isolated rabbit MPA, a CCK-8 assay was conducted over a 7-day culture period. The resulting curve (Figure 3(c)) displayed a sigmoidal pattern typical of primary adherent cells, comprising a lag phase, an active growth phase, and a plateau phase. During Days 1 to 3, metabolic activity gradually increased as the cells adapted to the in vitro environment and attached to the culture surface. From Days 3 to 5, the optical density (OD) at 450 nm increased more rapidly, indicating a significant expansion of viable and metabolically active preadipocytes. Although the cultures approached high morphological confluence by approximately 72 hours (Figure 3(a)), metabolic activity continued to rise, suggesting that contact inhibition had not yet fully suppressed cellular activity. From Days 5 to 7, the curve plateaued, reflecting growth limitations associated with confluence and reduced proliferation. Compared with porcine and bovine IMPA,27,28 rabbit cells transitioned to the plateau phase earlier, indicating greater sensitivity to confluence-dependent growth regulation or an inherently lower proliferative capacity. This earlier growth limitation may explain species-specific differences in IMF deposition and meat quality traits. It is important to note that OD 450 nm values indicate cellular metabolic activity and viability rather than direct cell number.

Due to the limited availability of validated species-specific antibodies for key surface markers in the rabbit model, a targeted qPCR strategy was employed to define the molecular identity of the isolated SVF. This approach directly compared the gene expression profile of the IMF-derived SVF to that of a pure dermal fibroblast population to evaluate preadipocyte enrichment and exclude major contaminants.

The IMF-SVF exhibited a distinct molecular signature compared to fibroblasts. Notably, the IMF-SVF was highly enriched for transcripts of the definitive preadipocyte markers PDGFRA and CD34, whereas fibroblasts showed minimal expression of these genes (Figure 3(b)). This PDGFRA+ CD34+ profile aligns with the established phenotype of adipogenic progenitor cells across species.29 Furthermore, the IMF-SVF, but not fibroblasts, expressed the muscle-niche marker ITGA7, confirming its anatomical origin within the muscle interstitium. The absence of the mature adipocyte marker ADIPOQ in both populations confirmed a lack of differentiated fat cell contamination, and the negligible expression of the myogenic regulator MYOD1 ruled out significant contamination by skeletal muscle progenitors.

These results demonstrate that, while the initial SVF is a heterogeneous isolate, the cultured population is transcriptionally defined and enriched for PDGFRA+ CD34+ adipogenic progenitors. This enrichment effectively minimizes concerns regarding fibroblast overgrowth, as the molecular profile of the cultured cells is distinct from that of dermal fibroblasts. The protocol thus provides a reliable method to obtain a progenitor population primed for adipogenic differentiation from rabbit intramuscular fat. For studies requiring absolute cellular purity, future work could employ fluorescence-activated cell sorting once a broader panel of rabbit-compatible antibodies becomes available. Nonetheless, the molecular signature presented here confirms that the isolated population is predominantly composed of adipogenic progenitor cells residing within the muscle niche, providing a validated cellular substrate for investigating the genetic and physiological regulation of intramuscular adipogenesis in a rabbit model.

To further characterize the isolated cells, we used RT-qPCR to analyze lineage-specific marker expression in passage 3 (P3) IMF-SVF-derived cells maintained under proliferative conditions before adipogenic induction. The expression of key preadipocyte markers (ZFP423, PREF1/DLK1, CD34, and PDGFRA) was evaluated relative to markers of myogenic (PAX7, MYOD1), fibroblastic (COL1A1), and hematopoietic (PTPRC) lineages. Expression levels were normalized to β-actin (Figure 3(d)). The isolated cells showed high expression of the preadipocyte markers PDGFRA, CD34, and ZFP423, but negligible expression of the myogenic, fibroblastic, and hematopoietic markers. These results confirm that we isolated a highly enriched IMPA population.

Consistent with its established role as an inhibitor of adipogenic commitment, PREF1/DLK1 displayed the highest relative expression among the genes analysed. High PREF1/DLK1 expression is a hallmark of the preadipocyte state and must be downregulated for differentiation to proceed.30 In contrast, the master regulators of terminal differentiation, C/EBPa and PPARγ, were expressed at low basal levels, indicating that the cells were maintained in a proliferative, non-differentiated state. Meanwhile, ZFP423, a transcription factor required for preadipocyte determination and competence, showed moderate expression.

This temporal gene expression pattern, high PREF1/DLK1 and ZFP423, followed by delayed upregulation of PPARG, C/EBPa, and FABP4, suggests active maintenance of the preadipocyte state and controlled initiation of differentiation. PREF1/DLK1 suppresses adipogenesis upstream of PPARG,31 while ZFP423 defines early adipogenic competence. Differentiation begins when C/EBPβ/δ activate PPARG and C/EBPa, leading to lipid accumulation. Previous studies in Wagyu cattle identified TGF-β/SMAD and extracellular matrix pathways as key inhibitory regulators of IMF adipogenesis.32 Upregulation of integrins (ITGA6, ITGB1) and GTPase signalling supports a microenvironmental brake on differentiation, while miRNAs such as bta-miR-493 targeting BMPR1A modulate BMP/TGFβ and p38-MAPK signaling.32 These insights suggest that rabbit IMPA may exhibit elevated anti-adipogenic signalling through the TGF-β or Wnt pathways, thereby delaying the full activation of PPARG. This hypothesis could be tested by applying agents such as rosiglitazone (a PPARG agonist), SB-431542 (a TGF-βR inhibitor), or IWR-1 (a Wnt inhibitor) to enhance differentiation in vitro.

sections.title: Morphological characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes

paragraphs.en: We characterized the morphological progression of primary cells isolated from the rabbit LD during early in vitro culture (Figure 3(a)). Within approximately 12 hours after enzymatic digestion, most cells were non-adherent, rounded, and suspended in the medium, aligning with the profile of freshly isolated preadipocytes observed in other livestock species. Cell attachment became evident between 12 and 48 h post-seeding, after which adherent cells displayed spindle-shaped, fibroblast-like morphology. The relatively low cell density observed in subsequent cultures reflects the initial plating density rather than impaired adhesive capacity. By 48 to 72 hours, the culture formed a confluent monolayer of spindle-shaped cells, with no detectable intracellular lipid droplets. The absence of spontaneous lipid accumulation ensures that the cell population is undifferentiated and suitable for controlled adipogenesis experiments. This is critical for interpreting results, as spontaneous differentiation would confound analyses of adipogenic regulators and interventions.33

sections.title: Immunofluorescence validation of adipogenic markers in undifferentiated and differentiated preadipocytes

paragraphs.en: Immunofluorescence staining was conducted on isolated stromal vascular cells under both undifferentiated and adipogenic differentiation conditions to examine the expression of key adipogenic markers, including leptin, PREF-1, and PPARγ, in rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes and to verify cell identity (Figure 4). The analysis revealed distinct stage-dependent differences in both the expression levels and subcellular localization of these markers between undifferentiated and early differentiated preadipocytes, consistent with progression toward the adipogenic lineage.

In undifferentiated cells (Figure 4(a)), leptin exhibited minimal or absent CY3 fluorescence, indicating a lack of adipokine production characteristic of preadipocytes.34 In contrast, PREF-1 displayed a detectable cytoplasmic signal, consistent with its role as a preadipocyte-associated factor that maintains cells in an undifferentiated, anti-adipogenic state. PPARγ staining in undifferentiated cells was weak and largely non-nuclear, suggesting that the core adipogenic transcriptional program was not yet activated. Corresponding RT-qPCR analysis confirmed that basal PPARγ transcript levels were notably lower than those of the preadipocyte marker PREF-1 (Figure 3(d)), suggesting that most cells had not yet fully differentiated. The detection of nuclear PPARγ in preadipocytes aligns with its reported role in early adipogenic lineage priming and commitment.35

Following induction of adipogenic differentiation (Figure 4(b)), marker expression changed considerably. Leptin showed a robust and diffuse cytoplasmic CY3 signal, reflecting the acquisition of adipocyte-like functional properties and the initiation of adipokine expression.34 PREF-1 expression was markedly reduced and heterogeneous across the cell population, consistent with its known downregulation during adipogenic commitment and the asynchronous nature of differentiation in primary intramuscular preadipocytes. PPARγ, in contrast, exhibited strong nuclear localization, indicating activation of the central adipogenic regulatory axis and transcriptional control of downstream lipid metabolism genes.

Taken together, the reciprocal expression of PREF-1 and PPARγ, along with the induction of leptin, indicates a clear transition from a preadipocyte state to early adipogenic differentiation. This coordinated expression pattern reflects the suppression of preadipocyte identity (PREF-1), the activation of the adipogenic transcriptional core (PPARγ), and the emergence of early adipocyte functional markers (leptin). This confirms that the isolated stromal vascular cells are bona fide preadipocytes that have successfully entered the adipogenic program. Consequently, these markers provide a reliable framework for distinguishing undifferentiated from early differentiated intramuscular preadipocytes.

sections.title: Morphological dynamics of rabbit intramuscular adipocyte differentiation in vitro

paragraphs.en: Following adipogenic induction, rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes underwent a progressive morphological transformation over 9 days (Figure 5(a)). On Day 0, the cells exhibited a fibroblast-like appearance with no visible intracellular inclusions, indicating an early lag phase before adipogenic commitment. By Day 3, the cells began to take on a more rounded shape, accompanied by small intracellular refractile structures consistent with early lipid accumulation. On Day 6, the size and number of these structures increased, suggesting enhanced lipid deposition as differentiation continued. By Day 9, many cells displayed a unilocular, signet-ring-like morphology typical of mature adipocyte droplets.36 Since bright-field imaging alone cannot definitively identify lipid droplets, these morphological changes were analyzed alongside adipogenic marker expression and lipid-specific staining (Figures 5(b–e) and 6), which collectively confirm successful adipogenic differentiation.

This defined in vitro differentiation timeline serves as a valuable cellular model for studying the genetic regulation of intramuscular adipogenesis in rabbits, including the expression of key regulatory genes such as PPARγ and FABP4 that contribute to marbling traits.

Adipocyte differentiation is a highly regulated, multistage process driven by a complex network of transcriptional and signalling events that transform preadipocytes into mature, lipid-laden adipocytes. To understand the molecular mechanisms underlying this process in rabbits, we profiled the temporal expression of four key adipogenic regulators: PREF1/DLK1, C/EBPa, PPARγ, and FABP4 during the in vitro differentiation of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes (Figure 5(b–e)). PREF1/DLK1 sharply declined following induction. Its continuous expression keeps cells in an undifferentiated state, while its downregulation is crucial for adipogenic progression.37 Mechanistically, PREF1/DLK1 interacts with fibronectin to activate the ERK/MAPK signaling cascade, which upregulates Sox9, a transcription factor that further represses C/EBPa and PPARγ, maintaining the anti-adipogenic state.31 In our study, the rapid decline in PREF1/DLK1 expression following induction confirms the successful initiation of adipogenesis in rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes.

C/EBPa and PPARG, the two master regulators of adipogenesis, significantly increased from Day 3 onward, peaking on Day 9. PPARγ serves as the central transcriptional activator governing lipid metabolism, adipocyte maturation, and insulin sensitivity.38 Its ectopic expression alone is sufficient to trigger adipocyte differentiation, while its absence prevents lipid accumulation and adipogenic gene expression.39 C/EBPa works synergistically with PPARG, establishing a positive feedback loop that reinforces their mutual expression and sustains the adipogenic phenotype.40 Together, these transcription factors coordinate the activation of genes involved in lipid droplet formation, fatty acid uptake, and adipokine secretion, hallmarks of terminal adipocyte differentiation. The concurrent upregulation of PPARG and C/EBPa in our study indicates the activation of canonical adipogenic pathways and the successful transition from early to terminal adipogenesis in rabbits. Similarly, FABP4 , a well-characterized late adipogenic marker, showed a significant increase starting on Day 3 and peaking at Day 9. FABP4 functions as a lipid chaperone that binds and transports long-chain fatty acids within adipocytes, facilitating lipid utilization, storage, and signaling.41 Its induction signifies the onset of lipid droplet formation and the establishment of mature adipocyte function. Inhibition of FABP4 has been shown to impair lipid droplet growth and reduce the number of mature adipocytes, emphasizing its necessity for terminal adipogenesis.41

Furthermore, a comparative analysis of adipogenic gene expression was conducted between undifferentiated preadipocytes (control) and preadipocytes at an early stage of differentiation (Figure 5(f)). The results revealed a distinct transcriptional signature indicative of adipogenic commitment. Specifically, the preadipocyte marker PREF1/DLK1 was significantly downregulated, indicating a transition from the undifferentiated state. Concurrently, the expression of key adipogenic regulators, including PPARG and C/EBPa, was significantly upregulated. Additionally, expression of the adipocyte marker FABP4 was markedly increased. This coordinated transcriptional shift, characterized by the repression of PREF1/DLK1 and the activation of the core adipogenic transcriptional network, indicates the successful initiation of the adipogenic differentiation program. These molecular changes precede and align with the subsequent accumulation of intracellular lipid droplets observed during later stages of differentiation.

In summary, the sequential expression pattern observed, with PREF1/DLK1 downregulation followed by the upregulation of C/EBPa, PPARG, and FABP4, demonstrates that rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes undergo a well-orchestrated differentiation process, consistent with findings in other mammalian models.42–46 These results confirm that our in vitro differentiation system accurately replicates the key molecular events of adipogenesis. Furthermore, the defined temporal dynamics of these transcription factors provide a robust framework for future investigations into the non-coding RNA-mediated regulation of intramuscular fat deposition in rabbits, which may have critical implications for improving meat quality and metabolic efficiency.

sections.title: Validation of lipid accumulation by Oil Red O staining

paragraphs.en: Oil Red O staining confirmed the biochemical progression of adipogenesis (Figure 6(a)). Day 0 cells exhibited no staining, whereas Day 3 cells showed sparse lipid droplets. By Day 6 of induction, cultured preadipocytes exhibited early signs of differentiation, characterized by the appearance of small intracellular lipid droplets, indicative of C/EBPα activation. By Day 9, substantial lipid accumulation was apparent, with larger and more numerous lipid droplets throughout the cytoplasm. On Day 12, the cells showed intense Oil Red O staining and extensive lipid accumulation, morphologically resembling mature adipocytes with large lipid inclusions that occupied most of the cytoplasmic space. Consistent with the morphological observations from Oil Red O staining, spectrophotometric quantification of extracted dye showed a progressive, time-dependent increase in lipid accumulation during adipogenic differentiation (Figure 6(b)). Relative absorbance values at 450 nm remained low on Day 0 and Day 3, with no significant difference compared to preadipocytes, which corresponded to the minimal lipid deposition observed microscopically. A moderate but significant increase was detected by Day 6, indicating the onset of intracellular lipid droplet formation. In contrast, a marked elevation in OD450 was observed on Days 9 and 12, signifying robust triglyceride accumulation and maturation of adipocytes, in agreement with the intense Oil Red O staining and extensive lipid droplet formation seen in the later stages of differentiation. This terminal differentiation phase was further supported by the expression of FABP4, a hallmark gene of mature adipocytes and a key indicator of late-stage adipogenesis.43

In summary, these results confirm that the isolated rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes successfully underwent differentiation in vitro, following the canonical adipogenic program characterized by the sequential activation of C/EBPα, PPARγ, and FABP4. This progression highlights the functional validity of our in vitro model for studying the molecular mechanisms underlying adipogenesis and IMF deposition in rabbits.

This study has limitations that suggest directions for future research. While the initialSVF is a heterogeneous isolate, our molecular characterization confirms that the cultured population is specifically enriched for PDGFRA+ CD34+ adipogenic progenitors and is distinct from dermal fibroblasts, alleviating concerns that contaminating cell types influence the results. However, the cells were derived from neonatal rabbits, and their differentiation potential may differ from that of cells isolated at production-relevant ages. Additionally, the sample size was limited to three individuals from a single breed (Hycole) and sex (male) at one time point. Future studies involving larger cohorts, diverse breeds, both sexes, and multiple developmental stages would enhance the generalizability of the findings. Finally, although we identified the predominant population as adipogenic progenitors, the potential presence of subpopulations, such as fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs), within the PDGFRα+ pool warrants further investigation. Future research using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) with a broader panel of markers, once species-specific reagents become available, could further refine population purity and elucidate distinct lineage contributions.

This study establishes a standardized and reproducible in-vitro model for rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes and delineates their morphological, molecular, and functional characteristics during adipogenesis. The sequential downregulation of PREF1 and upregulation of C/EBPα, PPARγ, and FABP4 confirm that rabbit IMPA follows a conserved mammalian adipogenic program, while the observed slower proliferation and delayed differentiation highlight species- and depot-specific regulatory features consistent with the lean phenotype of rabbits.

After washing in PBS containing 2% penicillin/streptomycin and removing the connective tissue, the muscle was minced into fragments of 1–3 mm³. figures.label: Figure 2.
figures.caption: Timeline of adipogenic induction in rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes.This schematic provides an overview of the differentiation protocol. Cells were cultured to 80–90% confluence by Day −2 and were then induced with adipogenic medium on Day 0. Maintenance medium was supplied on Day 2 and refreshed every 48 hours thereafter. Complete adipocyte differentiation was achieved by Day 12.

figures.caption: Cell morphology, proliferation ability, and gene expression of rabbit intramuscular preadipocyte. (a) Primary growth of preadipocytes in rabbit (12 hours, 24 hours, 48 hours, and 72 hours post isolation. Scale bar: 200 µm (applies to all panels). (b) Relative expression levels of marker genes were compared between pure intramuscular fibroblasts (control) and the SVF-derived cell population suspected to be intramuscular preadipocytes. Genes assessed include: ITGA7 (myogenic progenitor marker), CD34 and PDGFRA (preadipocyte/stromal markers), ADIPOQ (mature adipocyte marker), and MYOD1 (myoblast marker). Low expression of fibroblast and myogenic markers (ITGA7, MYOD1) alongside elevated expression of preadipocyte markers (CD34, PDGFRA) in the SVF population supports successful isolation and purity of preadipocytes with minimal contamination from fibroblasts or myogenic cells. Data are presented as mean ± SEM. (c) growth curve of rabbit preadipocyte cell using CCK8; (d) The relative mRNA expression of key lineage-specific markers in passage 3 (P3) IMF-SVF-derived cells maintained in the undifferentiated, proliferative state before adipogenic induction . Expression levels (mean ± SEM) were normalized to β-actin and compared to a calibrator sample. The profile confirms that the isolated cells are preadipocytes, as indicated by high expression of adipogenic markers (PPARG, PREF1/DLK1, Zfp423, PDGFRA). The negligible expression of the hematopoietic marker PTPRC (CD45) confirms the absence of immune cell contamination. Additionally, low expression levels of myocyte (MYOD1), osteocyte (Pax7), fibroblast (COL1A1), and mature adipocyte (ADIPOQ, C/EBPa) markers further support the preadipocyte lineage commitment and the purity of the isolated cell population. Data were obtained from n = 3 independent biological replicates.

figures.label: Figure 4.
figures.caption: Immunofluorescence analysis of adipogenic markers in SVF-derived preadipocytes before and after differentiation.Representative immunofluorescence images of SVF-derived cells in the undifferentiated preadipocyte state (A) and the differentiated preadipocyte state (B). Cells were stained for leptin (an adipokine marker), PREF-1 (a preadipocyte marker), and PPARγ (the master regulator of adipogenesis). Nuclei were counterstained with DAPI (blue), and specific antibody binding was detected in the CY3 channel (red). The merged images illustrate the cellular localization of each target protein. Undifferentiated cells exhibit strong PREF-1 expression with minimal leptin and PPARγ signals, whereas differentiated cells show reduced PREF-1 and increased leptin and PPARγ expression, consistent with adipogenic differentiation. Negative control images (secondary antibody only) confirmed the staining specificity. Scale bar: 200 µm (applies to all panels).

figures.label: Figure 5.
figures.caption: Morphology of cell and gene expression after induction of differentiation. (a) Representative micrographs illustrating the morphological changes at various time points during rabbit preadipocyte differentiation: (I) Day 0, (II) Day 3, (III) Day 6, and (IV) Day 9. (b) qPCR analysis displaying relative expression levels of adipogenic marker genes (PREF1/DLK1, FABP4, PPARγ, and C/EBPa) during differentiation, normalized to β-actin. Asterisks indicate significant differences (P < 0.05). (c-e) Temporal expression analysis of individual genes: Values are presented as means ± standard deviations, with different lowercase letters signifying significant differences (P < 0.05) across time points. (f) Relative mRNA levels of PREF1/DLK1 and PDGFRA (preadipocyte markers) and PPARG, ADIPOQ, and C/EBPa (adipogenic markers) in undifferentiated and differentiated rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes were quantified by qRT-PCR. Expression was normalized to β-actin using the 2^(-ΔΔCt) method. Data represent mean ± SEM (n ≥ 3). *P < 0.05; **P < 0.01.

figures.label: Figure 6.
figures.caption: Lipid accumulation in adipocytes assessed by Oil Red O staining.(a) Representative photomicrographs of preadipocyte (Pa) and adipocytes (day 0- day 12) stained with Oil Red O, which specifically targets neutral lipids. The red staining indicates the presence of intracellular lipid droplets. Scale bar, 200 µm (applies to all panels).(b) Quantitative analysis of lipid accumulation. Data are presented as mean ± SEM from n = 6 independent experiments. Significant differences between groups were determined using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s post-hoc test. p < 0.01.
